title: Unbounded generator degrees in moment ideals via graph faces
shortTitle: Moment equations have no uniform degree bound
oneLine: A constructive proof candidate embeds graph faces into full moment models, forcing equations of arbitrarily large necessary degree and producing an intrinsically nonnormal example.
abstract: For each r at least three, the full moment ideal with n=r squared and d=((r+1)^(r squared−2r+2)−1)/r cannot be generated by polynomials of degree below r. The proof packs binary edge-selection constraints into moment levels and uses an exposed face to exclude shortcuts through other coordinates. It extends to graph toric ideals and an intrinsically nonnormal moment variety. Exact finite checks support the self-contained argument; both model indices vary.
narration: How complicated must the equations of a statistical model become? Moments describe features such as averages and higher powers. When variables are independent, their joint moments satisfy polynomial equations. The question is whether one fixed degree limit could always suffice to generate those equations, no matter how large the model becomes. This unrefereed candidate gives a constructive negative answer. For any proposed limit, its written proof builds a full moment model requiring a higher-degree equation. The key object is an even cycle. It has exactly two ways to pair all its vertices using disjoint edges. The construction turns those matchings into two products of moment coordinates with the same parameter image. They share no factor, so their difference cannot come from lower-degree equations. Crucially, the proof also prevents all the other model coordinates from supplying a shortcut. A supporting functional isolates the cycle as an exposed face. The same construction works for more general graphs and produces a separate geometric consequence: an intrinsically nonnormal moment variety. These are structural results. The number of variables and the moment order both grow, and the construction uses very large parameters. It does not settle the fixed-dimension question or show that every statistical algorithm is difficult. Readers can inspect the complete written argument and rerun two exact finite implementations. Those computations support examples, not the infinite theorem. This is an unrefereed Evidence Press candidate dated September ninth, twenty twenty-six. The full paper and evidence are linked on the release page. This is an AI-generated voice summary, not additional mathematical evidence.

keyResults: An explicit necessary degree-r obstruction for every r at least three, with both n and d varying.
Every finite simple graph with an edge embeds as an exposed moment face preserving its graded toric ideal.
Nonempty binary equality configurations admit the specified complement-variable realization.
An explicit moment variety is intrinsically nonnormal, not merely non-projectively-normal.
evidence: Nine-page self-contained proof; two exact finite implementations; thirteen semantic controls; full normal/optimized certificate comparison; non-destructive replay regression; fresh-archive checks; internal editorial reports and bounded novelty audit.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate with a complete written argument as both n and d vary. Finite replay is supporting evidence, not universal certification. Fixed-n unboundedness, optimal parameters, historical priority, external review, formal verification and impact are not established.
openProblems: Reduce the very large encoded moment order and position count.
Determine whether necessary generator degrees are unbounded for a fixed number of variables.
Identify further graph-ring properties preserved by the moment-face realization.
Formalize the carry-free encoding, face retraction and full-fiber argument.
